output.question: Has Qualcomm announced layoffs?
output.answer: Yes. CEO Cristiano Amon told staff in an internal memo dated October 19, 2026 that Qualcomm will make global job cuts after its annual reviews. He framed them as performance-focused and said notifications would start in November 2026. The memo, which Reuters reviewed, gave no headcount, and Qualcomm had roughly 52,000 employees as of September 2025. On November 11, 2026, The Federal, citing the Financial Express, reported that India cuts began in Bengaluru on November 9 and that about 1,000 Indian jobs could be affected, with analysts expecting another round in January. That India figure is an analyst estimate, and Qualcomm has not officially commented on the India layoffs.

key_facts.fact: CEO Cristiano Amon announced global performance-focused job cuts in an internal memo to staff dated Monday, October 19, 2026, which Reuters reviewed.
Layoff notifications were to begin in November 2026, after annual employee reviews.
The memo did not give a number of job cuts, and Reuters could not determine the scale. Qualcomm had about 52,000 employees as of September 2025.

India cuts began at the Bengaluru facility on November 9, 2026 and will be phased across Hyderabad, Chennai and Delhi NCR. About 1,000 Indian jobs are expected to be affected, per an analyst estimate.
Analysts expect another round of cuts in January. Qualcomm has not officially commented on the India layoffs.

passages.quote: a stronger performance culture ... has consistently fallen short of expectations
We must have the right people in the right roles.
Qualcomm begins India layoffs as part of 'restructuring', to cut over 1,000 jobs

caveats: Qualcomm has not disclosed how many jobs it is cutting worldwide. Reports that about 7% of the global workforce could be affected are not confirmed by the company.
The roughly 1,000 India figure is an estimate from EIIRTrend analyst Pareekh Jain, which The Federal reported via the Financial Express. Qualcomm has not officially commented on it.
The announcement is an internal memo reported by Reuters, not a public press release or SEC filing, and Qualcomm did not respond to Reuters' request for comment.
Search results also mention an earlier April 2026 round of San Diego WARN notices covering about 105 workers, but I did not open those pages, so those figures are unverified.
The CNBC page quotes the memo only in fragments, so the passages above are short excerpts rather than full sentences.
